hypotheses.reasoning: Third-party geo-IP provider api.geoip.example began returning 502/503 at 21:27:29 (#110) with healthy traffic just before (#107,#108). Failures persisted (#114,#118), enrichment-svc's circuit breaker opened (#121), ingest-api got 503 circuit-open from enrichment (#138,#172), and the gateway returned 503s on POST /v1/events (#122+). A half-open probe still got 502 at 21:40 (#174). The provider responds immediately with errors (fail-fast 5xx), so this is an external outage, not a hang. No deploys. The disk warning (#15) came 11 minutes earlier and caused no errors.
The circuit breaker and synchronous enrichment dependency carry the provider failure to the edge. But the trigger is a real, ongoing provider outage, and I saw no retries making it worse.

verdict.recommendedAction: Confirm the outage on the geo-IP provider's status page and open a ticket citing x-request-ids ed00dda, 123ab60 and a20d31b. Meanwhile, stop enrichment from blocking ingestion: when the provider is down, have enrichment-svc fall back to geo-cache or return the event without enrichment, and have ingest-api accept events instead of passing the 503 back to callers. Consider a failover geo-IP provider. Separately, find out why gateway requests wait 7–29s before failing when enrichment-svc is answering immediately.
